_note: Roll table bank. Original Gazette text only (no SRD paste). die is 6 or 20 and rows must match it. status: draft until the owner approves a table.

tables.title: What's in the Goblin's Pocket?
tables.kicker: Searched after the ambush on the Tanner's Row road
rows: Three copper pieces and a fourth that is clearly a button
A tooth. Not a goblin tooth. Not a tooth of anyone nearby
A map of the road you are standing on, with your faces drawn on it
A half-eaten pie, still warm. Whose oven?
An IOU signed by a much bigger goblin
A tiny portrait of a goblin mother, signed “come home safe”
tables.question: Roll a d6 and tell us what you found. Then tell us what your party did about it.

tables.title: What's on the Notice Board?
tables.kicker: Nailed up outside the Sleeping Mule this morning
rows: Lost: one cat. Answers to nothing. Is on fire
Help wanted at the mill. Ask about the basement
Reward for the return of a stolen bell
Adventurers wanted. Must own their own shovel
The well is fine. Stop asking about the well
Bard seeks band. Lute player left suddenly
Found: one boot, foot still inside
Duel at dawn. Bring a second. And a third
Free goats. Do not ask why
Escort needed to the next town. Pays in pie
Missing: the bridge. Last seen on Tuesday
Lessons in swordplay. Bandages not included
Do not feed the thing under the stairs
Haunted chair for sale. Comfortable
Witness to the fire, please come forward
Wedding Friday. Groom still undecided
Ratcatcher wanted. Previous one eaten
Taxes due. The collector is armed now
A map, torn in half. The other half: inquire
Your own name, in your own handwriting
tables.question: Roll a d20. Which notice does your party take down, and which one should they have left alone?

tables.title: Why Is This Door Locked?
tables.kicker: A dungeon architect's guide to the third corridor
rows: To keep something in. It is still in there
To keep you out. It has been waiting a long time
The key-keeper died with the key, inside, behind the door
It isn't locked. It's being held shut from the other side
There is a very good treasure room behind it. Was
The dungeon's owner locks it every night out of habit
tables.question: Roll a d6. What does your rogue find when the lock gives?

tables.title: Who's in the Corner Booth?
tables.kicker: The table nobody at the Sleeping Mule sits at
rows: A hooded stranger. Obviously
A dwarf asleep in his own beard
Your party's last hireling
Two halflings in one long coat
A bard writing a song about you
A knight who lost a bet
A goblin with a very good fake mustache
Someone who looks just like your cleric
A tax collector, off duty, still counting
A ghost who hasn't noticed yet
A retired adventurer with one story
The tavern's cat, on a chair, paying
A wizard arguing with his hat
Three dice players. One always wins
A merchant selling maps to here
An orc reading poetry, crying a little
A child who says she owns the place
A mimic. It's the booth
A dragon in a very convincing hat
Nobody. The ale is still warm
tables.question: Roll a d20. Who's in the corner booth, and does your party go over and say hello?

tables.title: What Else Is in the Hoard?
tables.kicker: Not the gold. The other stuff
rows: A teacup. The dragon is very particular about it
Forty-one left boots, sorted by size
A knight in full armor, asleep since spring
Love letters from a second dragon
A bag of holding with another hoard in it
A bad portrait of the dragon, framed in gold
A crown nobody alive can place
Every key to the town gates
A ledger. The dragon has been lending money
One very nervous kobold accountant
A sword that will not stop apologizing
Your party's wanted posters, pinned up
The church bell from the next village
A wedding cake, uneaten, turned to stone
Seven copies of the same rare book
A rival adventurer's diary, last page blank
A cozy blanket. Do not touch the blanket
An egg. Warm
A mirror that shows the hoard twice as big
A map to a bigger dragon's hoard
tables.question: Roll a d20. What does your party carry out, and does the dragon notice?

tables.title: Why Did the Hireling Quit?
rows: Paid in exposure. Exposure to fire, mostly
Was asked to check for traps by walking ahead of everyone
The wizard keeps practicing fireball near the torch
Learned the last three torchbearers were also called “Torchbearer”
Was invited to split the bill but never the loot
Got a better offer. From the dragon
tables.question: Roll a d6. Then tell us the worst job your party ever gave a hireling.

tables.title: What's in Your Christmas Gift?
tables.kicker: The guild's Christmas gift swap. Names from a helmet
rows: Socks. Enchanted. They walk off at night
A ten-foot pole, wrapped. Badly
A fruitcake that counts as a weapon
A party portrait, one face scratched out
Rope. The giver is not subtle
A potion labeled only “Trust me”
A mimic. It's the box
A candle that won't go out. Ever. Help
A voucher for a shop that burned down
Earmuffs, for the banshee job
A scarf knit by the barbarian. It's a lot
One gold coin, regifted from last year
A snow globe with a tiny screaming wizard
A book on manners, from the bard. Pointed
A bag of holding. Empty. Probably
A puppy. An owlbear puppy
Dice that roll 1s for everyone but you
The cleric's IOU. For one resurrection
A cursed ring. Still a very nice ring
Exactly what you wanted. Nobody knows how
tables.question: Roll a d20. What did your character unwrap on Christmas morning, and who in the party gave it?

tables.title: The Party's New Year Resolution
tables.kicker: Sworn on a tankard at the Sleeping Mule, midnight
rows: Stop opening every chest. The second one this year bit the rogue
Pay the hirelings. On time. In actual coin
Never split the party again, starting after this split
Let the bard finish one whole song before throwing things
Keep a list of everyone we promised to come back for
Learn the innkeeper's name. It has been three years
tables.question: Roll a d6. Which resolution does your party break first, and how fast?
